continuous-loop-20260801-c5.finding: batch_size=1 (vs control default) made smoke p50 latency ~5.6x worse (3285ms -> 18550ms) and structural_similarity worse (0.056 -> 0.018) at this fixed 20-step budget. Consistent with more, smaller optimizer steps costing more wall time per fixed step count on CPU at fixture scale; not evidence the lever is broken, just not worth pursuing at this budget.

continuous-loop-20260801-c6.finding: grammar_completion_bounds again shows a small smoke p50 latency win (135.7ms) at fixture scale, same direction as c1's bounds arm, but rejected as non-positive because meaningful_program_rate=0.0 (mpr) stays below the 1/3 floor required for a latency-only win to count (quality-aware tradeoff gate).

conclusion: 2 more fixture-scale screening cycles, both non-positive. c5 shows batch_size=1 clearly hurting smoke latency at this fixed step budget (not pursued further). c6 repeats the c1 pattern: grammar_completion_bounds trims smoke p50 latency slightly but meaningful_program_rate=0.0 blocks it from counting as a quality-aware win at fixture n=3 -- consistent with a lever that needs a real (non-fixture) training run before its quality effect can be measured, not a harness bug.
next_priorities: Do not pursue batch_size=1 for latency at fixture scale (c5 finding)
Re-test grammar_completion_bounds once a non-fixture run can produce meaningful_program_rate>0 signal, to see if the small latency win holds under a real quality-held comparison
